verses.speaker: अर्जुन उवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
एवं सततयुक्ता ये भक्तास्त्वां पर्युपासते |
ये चाप्यक्षरमव्यक्तं तेषां के योगवित्तमाः || १ ||
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच |
एवं सततयुक्ता ये भक्तास्त्वां पर्युपासते |
ये चाप्यक्षरमव्यक्तं तेषां के योगवित्तमाः || १ ||
verses.transliteration:
arjuna uvāca |
evaṃ satatayuktā ye bhaktāstvāṃ paryupāsate |
ye cāpyakṣaramavyaktaṃ teṣāṃ ke yogavittamāḥ || 1 ||
verses.word_meanings: arjunaḥ uvāca—Arjuna said; evam—thus; satata-yuktāḥ—always steadfastly engaged; ye—those who; bhaktāḥ—devotees; tvām—You (personal form); paryupāsate—properly worship; ye—those who; ca api—and also; akṣaram—the imperishable; avyaktam—the unmanifest; teṣām—of them; ke—who; yoga-vit-tamāḥ—most versed in yoga / supreme knowers of yoga.
verses.translation: Arjuna said: Those devotees who, ever steadfast, thus worship You with personal devotion, and those who worship the Imperishable, Unmanifest Absolute—which of these is superior in the knowledge of Yoga?
verses.meaning: Arjuna initiates the twelfth chapter by asking Sri Krishna to resolve an essential question that bridges Chapter 11 (the vision of the Divine Form) and Chapter 12: Between the devotee who meditates upon the personal, loving form of God (Saguna-Sakara) with unalloyed love, and the introspective seeker who contemplates the formless, unmanifest Absolute (Nirguna-Nirakara Brahman), who is more exalted in yoga? This inquiry forms the basis for Lord Krishna's exposition on Bhakti Yoga as the direct, sovereign path to divine union.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मय्यावेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते |
श्रद्धया परयोपेतास्ते मे युक्ततमा मताः || २ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मय्यावेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते |
श्रद्धया परयोपेतास्ते मे युक्ततमा मताः || २ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
mayyāveśya mano ye māṃ nityayuktā upāsate |
śraddhayā parayopetāste me yuktatamā matāḥ || 2 ||
verses.word_meanings: śrī-bhagavān uvāca—the Supreme Lord said; mayi—in Me (the Personal Supreme); āveśya—fixing/absorbing; manaḥ—the mind; ye—those who; mām—Me; nitya-yuktāḥ—ever steadfastly united; upāsate—worship; śraddhayā—with faith; parayā—supreme/transcendental; upetāḥ—endowed; te—they; me—by Me; yukta-tamāḥ—most perfect in yoga; matāḥ—are considered.
verses.translation: The Supreme Lord said: Those who, fixing their minds on Me, worship Me with constant steadfastness and supreme faith, are considered by Me to be the most perfect in Yoga.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna directly answers Arjuna's inquiry by affirming that those who absorb their heart, consciousness, and love in His personal form (Mayyaveshya Mano) with unwavering transcendental faith (Shraddhaya Paraya) are the highest yogis (Yuktatamah). Devotion is not passive sentimentality; it is the total focusing of all mental faculties upon the Supreme Divine with pure affection and unwavering constancy.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ये त्वक्षरमनिर्देश्यमव्यक्तं पर्युपासते |
सर्वत्रगमचिन्त्यं च कूटस्थमचलं ध्रुवम् || ३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ये त्वक्षरमनिर्देश्यमव्यक्तं पर्युपासते |
सर्वत्रगमचिन्त्यं च कूटस्थमचलं ध्रुवम् || ३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
ye tvakṣaramanirdeśyamavyaktaṃ paryupāsate |
sarvatragamacintyaṃ ca kūṭasthamacalaṃ dhruvam || 3 ||
verses.word_meanings: ye—those who; tu—but; akṣaram—the imperishable; anirdeśyam—indefinable/inexpressible; avyaktam—the unmanifest; paryupāsate—worship/contemplate; sarvatra-gam—all-pervading; acintyam—inconceivable; ca—and; kūṭa-stham—changeless/rock-seated; acalam—immovable; dhruvam—eternal/firm.
verses.translation: Yet those who worship the Imperishable, the Indefinable, the Unmanifest, the All-Pervading, the Inconceivable, the Changeless, the Immovable, and the Eternal;
verses.meaning: Here Sri Krishna acknowledges the path of Jnana Yoga—contemplation of the formless, transcendental Brahman. The attributes described (Akshara, Anirdeshya, Avyakta, Sarvatraga, Achintya, Kutastha, Achala, Dhruva) convey the absolute reality beyond sensory perception and intellect. While this path is valid, it requires supreme mental transcendence and complete sensory mastery.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
संनियम्येन्द्रियग्रामं सर्वत्र समबुद्धयः |
ते प्राप्नुवन्ति मामेव सर्वभूतहिते रताः || ४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
संनियम्येन्द्रियग्रामं सर्वत्र समबुद्धयः |
ते प्राप्नुवन्ति मामेव सर्वभूतहिते रताः || ४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
saṃniyamyendriyagrāmaṃ sarvatra samabuddhayaḥ |
te prāpnuvanti māmeva sarvabhūtahite ratāḥ || 4 ||
verses.word_meanings: saṃniyamya—subduing/restraining; indriya-grāmam—the entire aggregate of the senses; sarvatra—everywhere; sama-buddhayaḥ—even-minded / with equal vision; te—they; prāpnuvanti—attain; mām—Me; eva—alone; sarva-bhūta-hite—in the welfare of all beings; ratāḥ—actively engaged/delighting.
verses.translation: By fully subduing all the senses, maintaining evenness of mind under all circumstances, and actively rejoicing in the welfare of all living beings, they too attain Me alone.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna confirms that Jnana Yogis also ultimately reach the same Supreme Goal, provided they achieve complete mastery over the senses (Sanniyamyendriyagramam), maintain equanimity in all conditions (Sarvatra Samabuddhaya), and dedicate themselves to the selfless welfare of all creatures (Sarva-bhuta-hite ratah). Compassion and universal brotherhood are not opposed to non-dual wisdom, but are its natural fruit.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
क्लेशोऽधिकतरस्तेषामव्यक्तासक्तचेतसाम् |
अव्यक्ता हि गतिर्दुःखं देहवद्भिरवाप्यते || ५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
क्लेशोऽधिकतरस्तेषामव्यक्तासक्तचेतसाम् |
अव्यक्ता हि गतिर्दुःखं देहवद्भिरवाप्यते || ५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
kleśo'dhikarasteṣāmavyaktāsaktacetasām |
avyaktā hi gatirduḥkhaṃ dehavadbhiravāpyate || 5 ||
verses.word_meanings: kleśaḥ—trouble/distress; adhika-taraḥ—far greater; teṣām—of those; avyakta-āsakta-cetasām—whose minds are attached to the unmanifest; avyaktā—the unmanifest path; hi—indeed; gatiḥ—goal/way; duḥkham—with great difficulty/pain; dehavadbhiḥ—by embodied souls; avāpyate—is attained.
verses.translation: Greater is the toil of those whose minds are attached to the Unmanifest; for the unmanifest path is attained only with immense hardship by embodied beings.
verses.meaning: This is a pivotal philosophical declaration in the Bhagavad Gita. For living souls who are embodied (Dehavadbhih)—identified with mind, senses, and body—meditating upon a formless, attribute-less void or absolute consciousness without a concrete anchor is extraordinarily strenuous and fraught with spiritual obstacles. The Personal path (Bhakti) provides an innate, loving relationship with the Divine that naturally purifies and uplifts the embodied soul.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ये तु सर्वाणि कर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्पराः |
अनन्येनैव योगेन मां ध्यायन्त उपासते || ६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ये तु सर्वाणि कर्माणि मयि संन्यस्य मत्पराः |
अनन्येनैव योगेन मां ध्यायन्त उपासते || ६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
ye tu sarvāṇi karmāṇi mayi saṃnyasya matparāḥ |
ananyenaiva yogena māṃ dhyāyanta upāsate || 6 ||
verses.word_meanings: ye—those who; tu—but; sarvāṇi—all; karmāṇi—actions; mayi—unto Me; saṃnyasya—surrendering/renouncing; mat-parāḥ—regarding Me as the Supreme Goal; ananyena—unalloyed/undivided; eva—indeed; yogena—with yoga; mām—upon Me; dhyāyantaḥ—meditating; upāsate—worship.
verses.translation: But those who surrender all their actions unto Me, regarding Me as the Supreme Goal, and meditate upon Me with unswerving, single-minded devotion;
verses.meaning: In contrast to the grueling impersonal discipline, the devotee consecrates every mundane and spiritual activity unto Sri Krishna. By establishing an unbroken mental bond of exclusive love (Ananyenaiva Yogena), the devotee lives in joyful communion with the Divine in every heartbeat and deed.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तेषामहं समुद्धर्ता मृत्युसंसारसागरात् |
भवामि नचिरात्पार्थ मय्यावेशितचेतसाम् || ७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तेषामहं समुद्धर्ता मृत्युसंसारसागरात् |
भवामि नचिरात्पार्थ मय्यावेशितचेतसाम् || ७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
teṣāmahaṃ samuddhartā mṛtyusaṃsārasāgarāt |
bhavāmi nacirātpārtha mayyāveśitacetasām || 7 ||
verses.word_meanings: teṣām—for them; aham—I; samuddhartā—the deliverer/rescuer; mṛtyu-saṃsāra-sāgarāt—from the ocean of death-bound worldly existence (samsara); bhavāmi—I become; nacirāt—swiftly/without delay; pārtha—O son of Pritha (Arjuna); mayi—in Me; āveśita-cetasām—of those whose minds are absorbed.
verses.translation: For those whose minds are absorbed in Me, O Partha, I swiftly become their saviour, delivering them from the ocean of death and repeated mortal existence.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna offers one of the most comforting and compassionate assurances in all Vedic literature. The seeker of the unmanifest must swim across the ocean of samsara through grueling self-effort; but for the sincere bhakta whose heart is absorbed in Krishna, the Supreme Lord Himself steps in as the Divine Rescuer (Samuddharta), carrying them across the ocean of mortality without delay.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मय्येव मन आधत्स्व मयि बुद्धिं निवेशय |
निवसिष्यसि मय्येव अत ऊर्ध्वं न संशयः || ८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मय्येव मन आधत्स्व मयि बुद्धिं निवेशय |
निवसिष्यसि मय्येव अत ऊर्ध्वं न संशयः || ८ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
mayyeva mana ādhatsva mayi buddhiṃ niveśaya |
nivasiṣyasi mayyeva ata ūrdhvaṃ na saṃśayaḥ || 8 ||
verses.word_meanings: mayi eva—in Me alone; manaḥ—the mind; ādhatsva—fix/place; mayi—in Me; buddhim—the intellect/discernment; niveśaya—direct/absorb; nivasiṣyasi—you shall abide/dwell; mayi eva—in Me alone; ataḥ ūrdhvam—hereafter/beyond this life; na—no; saṃśayaḥ—doubt.
verses.translation: Fix your mind on Me alone, and absorb your intellect in Me. Thereafter, you shall undoubtedly live in Me forever.
verses.meaning: Here Sri Krishna begins His sublime 'ladder of spiritual alternatives'. The highest, most direct spiritual practice is to effortlessly surrender both feeling (mind/manas) and discernment (intellect/buddhi) into the Divine. When both emotional longing and rational intellect are centered on Krishna, one dwells in God consciousness even while engaged in worldly duty, with no doubt of eternal liberation.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अथ चित्तं समाधातुं न शक्नोषि मयि स्थिरम् |
अभ्यासयोगेन ततो मामिच्छाप्तुं धनञ्जय || ९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अथ चित्तं समाधातुं न शक्नोषि मयि स्थिरम् |
अभ्यासयोगेन ततो मामिच्छाप्तुं धनञ्जय || ९ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
atha cittaṃ samādhātuṃ na śaknoṣi mayi sthiram |
abhyāsayogena tato māmicchāptuṃ dhanañjaya || 9 ||
verses.word_meanings: atha—if however; cittam—the mind/consciousness; samādhātum—to steadily fix; na—not; śaknoṣi—you are able; mayi—in Me; sthiram—steadily/firmly; abhyāsa-yogena—by the yoga of constant practice; tataḥ—then; mām—Me; iccha—seek/desire; āptum—to attain; dhanañjaya—O conqueror of wealth (Arjuna).
verses.translation: If, however, you are unable to fix your mind steadily on Me, then seek to attain Me, O Dhananjaya, through the yoga of persistent practice (Abhyasa Yoga).
verses.meaning: Understanding human frailty, Sri Krishna gives the next rung of the ladder. If the mind wanders due to past conditioning (samskaras), one must practice Abhyasa Yoga—patiently bringing the straying mind back to contemplation of God whenever it drifts towards sensory objects (as taught in BG 6.26).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अभ्यासेऽप्यसमर्थोऽसि मत्कर्मपरमो भव |
मदर्थमपि कर्माणि कुर्वन्सिद्धिमवाप्स्यसि || १० ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अभ्यासेऽप्यसमर्थोऽसि मत्कर्मपरमो भव |
मदर्थमपि कर्माणि कुर्वन्सिद्धिमवाप्स्यसि || १० ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
abhyāse'pyasamartho'si matkarmaparamo bhava |
madarthamapi karmāṇi kurvansiddhimavāpsyasi || 10 ||
verses.word_meanings: abhyāse—in practice; api—even; asamarthaḥ—unable/unsuccessful; asi—you are; mat-karma-paramaḥ—dedicated to My service/work; bhava—become; mat-artham—for My sake; api—even; karmāṇi—actions/duties; kurvan—performing; siddhim—perfection/liberation; avāpsyasi—you shall attain.
verses.translation: If you are incapable even of persistent practice, then dedicate yourself to performing actions for My sake. Even by performing work for Me, you shall attain the highest perfection.
verses.meaning: If systematic meditation and mental concentration remain elusive, Sri Krishna offers devotional action (Mat-karma-paramo bhava). Performing actions for God's sake—temple service, singing praises, reading scriptures, helping fellow living beings as manifestations of God—purifies the subconscious mind and leads directly to spiritual perfection.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अथैतदप्यशक्तोऽसि कर्तुं मद्योगमाश्रितः |
सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं ततः कुरु यतात्मवान् || ११ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अथैतदप्यशक्तोऽसि कर्तुं मद्योगमाश्रितः |
सर्वकर्मफलत्यागं ततः कुरु यतात्मवान् || ११ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
athaitadapyasakto'si kartuṃ madyogamāśritaḥ |
sarvakarmaphalatyāgaṃ tataḥ kuru yatātmavān || 11 ||
verses.word_meanings: atha—if; etat—this; api—even; aśaktaḥ—incapable; asi—you are; kartum—to do; mat-yogam—refuge in My yoga; āśritaḥ—taking refuge; sarva-karma-phala-tyāgam—renunciation of the fruits of all actions; tataḥ—then; kuru—do/perform; yata-ātmavān—self-controlled.
verses.translation: If you are unable even to do this, taking refuge in devotion to Me, then, with a self-controlled mind, renounce the fruits of all your actions (Sarva-karma-phala-tyaga).
verses.meaning: Even if one cannot directly conscious-worship or dedicate sacred work to God, one can practice Karma Yoga: performing daily duties dutifully while surrendering attachment to the fruits and outcomes of actions. Renouncing selfish desire cleanses the heart of greed, anxiety, and ego.
verses.purport: Even if one cannot directly conscious-worship or dedicate sacred work to God, one can practice Karma Yoga: performing daily duties dutifully while surrendering attachment to the fruits and outcomes of actions. Renouncing selfish desire cleanses the heart of greed, anxiety, and ego.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
श्रेयो हि ज्ञानमभ्यासाज्ज्ञानाद्ध्यानं विशिष्यते |
ध्यानात्कर्मफलत्यागस्त्यागाच्छान्तिरनन्तरम् || १२ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
श्रेयो हि ज्ञानमभ्यासाज्ज्ञानाद्ध्यानं विशिष्यते |
ध्यानात्कर्मफलत्यागस्त्यागाच्छान्तिरनन्तरम् || १२ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
śreyo hi jñānamabhyāsājjñānāddhyānaṃ viśiṣyate |
dhyānātkarmaphalatyāgastyāgācchāntiranantaram || 12 ||
verses.word_meanings: śreyaḥ—better; hi—indeed; jñānam—knowledge/spiritual wisdom; abhyāsāt—than mere mechanical practice; jñānāt—than knowledge; dhyānam—meditation; viśiṣyate—is superior; dhyānāt—than meditation; karma-phala-tyāgaḥ—renunciation of the fruits of action; tyāgāt—from such renunciation; śāntiḥ—peace; anantaram—immediately follows.
verses.translation: Better indeed is spiritual knowledge than mechanical practice; superior to knowledge is meditation; higher than meditation is the renunciation of the fruits of action; for upon renunciation, immediate peace ensues.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna summarizes the hierarchy of practical spiritual disciplines. Blind mechanical ritual without understanding is lowest; cultivating spiritual wisdom (Jnana) is higher; integrating wisdom into deep meditation (Dhyana) is higher still; but renouncing the anxious craving for results (Karma-phala-tyaga) instantly bestows profound inner tranquility (Shanti) by eliminating the root cause of mental turbulence.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च |
निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः समदुःखसुखः क्षमी || १३ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अद्वेष्टा सर्वभूतानां मैत्रः करुण एव च |
निर्ममो निरहङ्कारः समदुःखसुखः क्षमी || १३ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
adveṣṭā sarvabhūtānāṃ maitraḥ karuṇa eva ca |
nirmamo nirahaṅkāraḥ samaduḥkhasukhaḥ kṣamī || 13 ||
verses.word_meanings: adveṣṭā—free from malice/hatred; sarva-bhūtānām—toward all living beings; maitraḥ—friendly; karuṇaḥ—compassionate; eva ca—and also; nirmamaḥ—free from possessiveness / 'mine-ness'; nirahaṅkāraḥ—free from egoism / 'I-ness'; sama-duḥkha-sukhaḥ—equipoised in sorrow and happiness; kṣamī—forgiving/patient.
verses.translation: He who harbours no malice toward any living being, who is friendly and compassionate, free from possessiveness and egoism, even-minded in pleasure and pain, and ever forgiving;
verses.meaning: Verses 12.13 to 12.20 describe the sublime 'Ashtadasha Lakshana' (qualities of the dear devotee). The true bhakta radiates universal friendliness (Maitra) and boundless empathy (Karuna), never holds resentment toward any creature (Adveshta), is free from false ownership (Nirmama) and pride (Nirahankara), and remains serene amid life's dualities with patient forgiveness (Kshami).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सन्तुष्टः सततं योगी यतात्मा दृढनिश्चयः |
मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः || १४ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
सन्तुष्टः सततं योगी यतात्मा दृढनिश्चयः |
मय्यर्पितमनोबुद्धिर्यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः || १४ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
santuṣṭaḥ satataṃ yogī yatātmā dṛḍhaniścayaḥ |
mayyarpitamanobuddhīryo madbhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ || 14 ||
verses.word_meanings: santuṣṭaḥ—contented; satatam—always; yogī—the yogi/devotee; yata-ātmā—self-controlled; dṛḍha-niścayaḥ—of firm conviction/determination; mayi—in Me; arpita-manaḥ-buddhiḥ—one whose mind and intellect are surrendered; yaḥ—whoever; mat-bhaktaḥ—My devotee; saḥ—that person; me—to Me; priyaḥ—is exceedingly dear.
verses.translation: That devotee who is ever contented, constantly united in yoga, self-controlled, firm in conviction, and whose mind and intellect are surrendered unto Me—he is exceedingly dear to Me.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna loves the devotee whose inner joy depends not on external wealth, but on inner spiritual contentment (Santushtah Satatam). With resolute faith (Dridha-nishchaya) and both intellect and heart dedicated to the Divine (Mayyarpita-mano-buddhih), this devotee becomes Krishna's beloved companion.

With resolute faith (Dridha-nishchaya) and both intellect and heart dedicated to the Divine (Mayyarpita-mano-buddhih), this devotee becomes Krishna's beloved companion.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः |
हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः || १५ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यस्मान्नोद्विजते लोको लोकान्नोद्विजते च यः |
हर्षामर्षभयोद्वेगैर्मुक्तो यः स च मे प्रियः || १५ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yasmānnodvijate loko lokānnodvijate ca yaḥ |
harṣāmarṣabhayodvegairmukto yaḥ sa ca me priyaḥ || 15 ||
verses.word_meanings: yasmāt—by whom; na—not; udvijate—is agitated/distressed; lokaḥ—the world/people; lokāt—by the world; na—not; udvijate—is agitated; ca—and; yaḥ—who; harṣa-amarṣa-bhaya-udvegaiḥ—from excited joy, envy/anger, fear, and anxiety; muktaḥ—freed; yaḥ—who; saḥ—he; ca—also; me—to Me; priyaḥ—is dear.
verses.translation: He by whom the world is not agitated, and who is not agitated by the world, who is freed from excitement, envy, fear, and anxiety—he is dear to Me.
verses.meaning: The spiritual saint is neither an agitator nor easily agitated. Their presence radiates calm, bringing comfort rather than disruption to society. Furthermore, when the chaos of the world lashes against them, they remain unperturbed, having conquered the turbulent emotional storms of elation (Harsha), resentment (Amarsha), dread (Bhaya), and anxiety (Udvega).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अनपेक्षः शुचिर्दक्ष उदासीनो गतव्यथः |
सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः || १६ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
अनपेक्षः शुचिर्दक्ष उदासीनो गतव्यथः |
सर्वारम्भपरित्यागी यो मद्भक्तः स मे प्रियः || १६ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
anapekṣaḥ śucirdakṣa udāsīno gatavyathaḥ |
sarvārambhaparityāgī yo madbhaktaḥ sa me priyaḥ || 16 ||
verses.word_meanings: anapekṣaḥ—free from worldly expectations/desires; śuciḥ—pure (internally and externally); dakṣaḥ—expert/diligent; udāsīnaḥ—impartial/unaffected; gatavyathaḥ—free from distress/grief; sarva-ārambha-parityāgī—renouncer of all ego-driven undertakings; yaḥ—who; mat-bhaktaḥ—My devotee; saḥ—he; me—to Me; priyaḥ—is dear.
verses.translation: He who is free from worldly expectations, pure within and without, skillful, impartial, free from distress, and who has renounced all ego-motivated undertakings—such a devotee of Mine is dear to Me.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna highlights an important harmony: The devotee is unattached (Anapeksha) yet expert and diligent in duties (Daksha). Purity of thought and action (Shuchi), freedom from partisan bias (Udasina), emotional resilience (Gatavyatha), and freedom from selfish, ego-driven ventures (Sarvarambha-parityagi) characterize the enlightened bhakta.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यो न हृष्यति न द्वेष्टि न शोचति न काङ्क्षति |
शुभाशुभपरित्यागी भक्तिमान्यः स मे प्रियः || १७ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
यो न हृष्यति न द्वेष्टि न शोचति न काङ्क्षति |
शुभाशुभपरित्यागी भक्तिमान्यः स मे प्रियः || १७ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
yo na hṛṣyati na dveṣṭi na śocati na kāṅkṣati |
śubhāśubhaparityāgī bhaktimānyaḥ sa me priyaḥ || 17 ||
verses.word_meanings: yaḥ—who; na—neither; hṛṣyati—rejoices unduly; na—nor; dveṣṭi—grieves/hates; na—nor; śocati—laments; na—nor; kāṅkṣati—craves/hopes for worldly gains; śubha-aśubha-parityāgī—renouncer of both pleasant and unpleasant karmic reactions; bhaktimān—full of devotion; yaḥ—who; saḥ—he; me—to Me; priyaḥ—is dear.
verses.translation: He who neither rejoices excessively over mundane gains nor hates what is unpleasant, who neither grieves over loss nor craves the unobtained, and who has renounced both good and evil fortunes—such a devoted soul is dear to Me.
verses.meaning: A devotee who has tasted the nectar of divine communion transcends the emotional swings of the material world. Because their soul is anchored in Sri Krishna, worldly windfalls do not intoxicate them, and misfortunes do not break their spirit. They view both pleasant and unpleasant events as aspects of divine will.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च तथा मानापमानयोः |
शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु समः सङ्गविवर्जितः || १८ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
समः शत्रौ च मित्रे च तथा मानापमानयोः |
शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु समः सङ्गविवर्जितः || १८ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
samaḥ śatrau ca mitre ca tathā mānāpamānayoḥ |
śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkheṣu samaḥ saṅgavivarjitaḥ || 18 ||
verses.word_meanings: samaḥ—equal/balanced; śatrau—toward enemy; ca—and; mitre—toward friend; ca—and; tathā—also; māna-apamānayoḥ—in honour and dishonour; śīta-uṣṇa-sukha-duḥkheṣu—in cold, heat, pleasure, and pain; samaḥ—equipoised; saṅga-vivarjitaḥ—free from all attachment.
verses.translation: He who is equal toward friend and foe, balanced in honour and dishonour, unaffected by cold, heat, pleasure, and pain, and completely free from all material attachments;
verses.meaning: Verses 18 and 19 describe the perfected state of equanimity (Samatvam). The bhakta looks beyond external societal labels of friend or adversary, recognising the indwelling Divinity in all beings. Praise and censure, heat and cold, prosperity and hardship are met with an unwavering, serene spirit.

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तुल्यनिन्दास्तुतिर्मौनी सन्तुष्टो येन केनचित् |
अनिकेतः स्थिरमतिर्भक्तिमान्मे प्रियो नरः || १९ ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
तुल्यनिन्दास्तुतिर्मौनी सन्तुष्टो येन केनचित् |
अनिकेतः स्थिरमतिर्भक्तिमान्मे प्रियो नरः || १९ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
tulyanindāstutirmaunī santuṣṭo yena kenacit |
aniketaḥ sthiramatirbhaktimānme priyo naraḥ || 19 ||
verses.word_meanings: tulya-nindā-stutiḥ—equal to blame and praise; maunī—contemplative/silent of speech; santuṣṭaḥ—content; yena kenacit—with whatever comes of its own accord; aniketaḥ—without attachment to a permanent home / viewing the universe as home; sthira-matiḥ—of steady intellect; bhaktimān—endowed with devotion; me—to Me; priyaḥ—dear; naraḥ—a human being.
verses.translation: He who treats blame and praise alike, who is quiet and contemplative, content with whatever comes by chance, unattached to a fixed dwelling, and firm in spiritual intellect—such a devoted person is dear to Me.
verses.meaning: The word 'Mauni' signifies not merely physical silence, but the silence of the ego and mastery over speech. 'Aniketa' signifies that the devotee does not derive their sense of identity or security from a house or earthly property, but finds their eternal home in the lotus feet of Sri Krishna with an unshakable intellect (Sthiramatih).

verses.speaker: श्रीभगवानुवाच
verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ये तु धर्म्यामृतमिदं यथोक्तं पर्युपासते |
श्रद्दधाना मत्परमा भक्तास्तेऽतीव मे प्रियाः || २० ||
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
ये तु धर्म्यामृतमिदं यथोक्तं पर्युपासते |
श्रद्दधाना मत्परमा भक्तास्तेऽतीव मे प्रियाः || २० ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
ye tu dharmyāmṛtamidaṃ yathoktaṃ paryupāsate |
śraddadhānā matparamā bhaktāste'tīva me priyāḥ || 20 ||
verses.word_meanings: ye—those who; tu—indeed; dharmya-amṛtam—immortal nectar of righteous wisdom (dharma); idam—this; yathā-uktam—as declared above; paryupāsate—faithfully follow and practice; śraddadhānāḥ—endowed with living faith; mat-paramāḥ—holding Me as the Supreme Goal; bhaktāḥ—devotees; te—they; atīva—supremely/exceedingly; me—to Me; priyāḥ—are dear.
verses.translation: Those who cherish and practice this immortal nectar of Dharma (Dharmyamritam) as declared above, endowed with deep faith and holding Me as the Supreme Goal—such devotees are supremely dear to Me.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna concludes the glorious twelfth chapter by describing the teaching of Bhakti as 'Dharmyamritam'—the immortal nectar of eternal spiritual truth. Whoever adopts these divine virtues with sincere faith (Shraddhadhana) and makes Sri Krishna their supreme refuge (Matparama) is not merely dear (Priya), but supremely and exceedingly dear (Ativa Priya) to the Lord. Thus culminates the path of pure loving devotion.
